# A Review of Developmental Interpretability in Large Language Models

**Kendiukhov — "A Review of Developmental Interpretability in Large Language Models"** · arXiv:2508.15841 (v1) · serialisation: recovered from the PDF (pymupdf, a PDF-only submission; the details of the conversion's provenance are at the head of the `original/` file).

**An external work; the abstract is given.** A review of the field of developmental interpretability (the interpretability of the training process rather than of a finished model). Grokking is given one paragraph with one reference; what the corpus values here is the external frame and the summary of the method's limits. Set aside by the triage of task-021 (2026-08-26). No work of the corpus cites it yet. The introduction and the quoted paragraphs are translated lazily, as quotations appear (decision D2-b). The original — [`original/`](original/2508.15841.a-review-of-developmental-interpretability-in-large-language-models.md); the analysis of the claims is the neighbouring `…claims.txt`.

# Abstract

*"This review synthesizes the nascent but critical field of developmental interpretability for Large Language Models (LLMs). We chart the field's evolution from static, post-hoc analysis of trained models to a dynamic investigation of the training process itself. We begin by surveying the foundational methodologies—including representational probing, causal tracing, and circuit analysis—that enable researchers to deconstruct the learning process. The core of this review examines the developmental arc of LLM capabilities, detailing key findings on the formation and composition of computational circuits, the biphasic nature of knowledge acquisition, the transient dynamics of learning strategies like in-context learning, and the phenomenon of emergent abilities as phase transitions in training. We explore illuminating parallels with human cognitive and linguistic development, which provide valuable conceptual frameworks for understanding LLM learning. Finally, we argue that this developmental perspective is not merely an academic exercise but a cornerstone of proactive AI safety, offering a pathway to predict, monitor, and align the processes by which models acquire their capabilities. We conclude by outlining the grand challenges facing the field, such as scalability and automation, and propose a research agenda for building more transparent, reliable, and beneficial AI systems."*
